title: Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs
focus: Graph ratio relationships and interpret ordered pairs

items.stem: Which of the following pairs of ratios are equivalent?
The graph shows points (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which statement best describes the relationship between the two quantities graphed? Show or explain your work.
choices: The ratios are not equivalent because the points do not form a straight line.
The ratios are equivalent because each y-value is 3 times the x-value.
The ratios are equivalent because each x-value is half the y-value.
The ratios are not equivalent because the points do not increase by the same amount.

items.stem: Select ALL statements that are true about equivalent ratios represented on a graph.
choices: Equivalent ratios form points that lie on the same straight line through the origin.
The ordered pairs representing equivalent ratios have the same ratio between their x- and y-values.
Equivalent ratios can be identified by comparing the differences between x-values on the graph.
If two ratios are equivalent, their points on the graph will always have the same x-values.

items.stem: A graph shows the points (3, 9) and (6, 18). Explain whether these two points represent equivalent ratios. Show or explain your work.
